screening_decisions.reason: In vitro mechanistic study examining drug effects on Na+ channels expressed in mammalian cells. Not a clinical trial in human patients with epilepsy.
Observational prospective cohort study of 525 patients with newly diagnosed epilepsy. Not a randomised controlled trial comparing phenobarbitone vs phenytoin monotherapy.

Double-blind study comparing multiple antiepileptic drugs including phenobarbital (phenobarbitone) and diphenylhydantoin (phenytoin) in patients with focal brain damage and epilepsy. While it includes additional drugs beyond the two of interest, it does contain a comparison between phenobarbitone and phenytoin in patients with focal seizures. Conservative inclusion recommended for full-text review.
Cochrane Review protocol focusing on teratogenic effects of AEDs in pregnancy. Not a primary RCT comparing phenobarbitone vs phenytoin monotherapy for seizure control.
Review article/guideline discussing general principles of AED therapy. Not a primary research study or RCT.
Epidemiological survey estimating prevalence/incidence of various neurologic disorders including epilepsy. Not a clinical trial comparing treatments.

Explicitly a randomised controlled trial comparing phenobarbital vs phenytoin as monotherapy in children aged 2-18 years with partial (focal) and generalised tonic-clonic epilepsy. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, correct interventions (phenobarbitone vs phenytoin), correct population (children with focal and/or generalised tonic-clonic seizures), monotherapy setting.
Methodological paper describing statistical techniques for meta-analysis. Not a clinical trial.
Meta-analysis estimating global prevalence of epilepsy. Not a primary RCT comparing phenobarbitone vs phenytoin.
Randomised controlled trial but compares phenobarbital vs carbamazepine, NOT phenobarbital vs phenytoin. Wrong intervention comparison per selection criteria.
Prospective observational study examining teratogenic effects of phenytoin and carbamazepine in pregnancy. Not a RCT comparing phenobarbitone vs phenytoin for seizure control.
Epidemiological/observational study describing natural history and prevalence of epilepsy in Denmark. Not a clinical trial.
Epidemiological study measuring incidence rates of epilepsy in HMO populations. Not a clinical trial comparing treatments.
Review article summarizing literature on behavioral and cognitive effects of AEDs in children. Not a primary RCT.
Methodological chapter from a book/manual about assessing risk of bias in systematic reviews. Not a clinical trial.
Observational registry study examining teratogenic effects of various AEDs in pregnancy. Not a RCT comparing phenobarbitone vs phenytoin monotherapy for seizure control.
Review article discussing diagnostic accuracy and case ascertainment methods in epilepsy epidemiology. Not a clinical trial.
Review article about dermatological uses and side effects of phenytoin. Not a clinical trial comparing phenobarbitone vs phenytoin for epilepsy.
In vitro mechanistic study examining GABA receptor modulation by carbamazepine and phenytoin in cell cultures. Not a clinical trial in human patients.
Animal study (rats) examining folate metabolism with different phenytoin formulations. Not a clinical trial in human patients with epilepsy.
Prospective cohort study, not an RCT. Does not compare phenobarbitone vs phenytoin monotherapy.
RCT comparing phenytoin and phenobarbitone monotherapy (along with carbamazepine). Includes both drugs of interest as monotherapy in epilepsy patients.
Combination therapy study (carbamazepine + phenobarbital/phenytoin), not monotherapy comparison.
RCT comparing phenobarbital and phenytoin monotherapy (along with carbamazepine and primidone) in adults with partial and secondarily generalized tonic-clonic seizures.
Methodological paper about meta-analysis techniques, not a primary RCT.
RCT comparing phenobarbitone and phenytoin monotherapy (along with sodium valproate) in children with generalized tonic-clonic convulsions.
Methodological paper about outcome reporting bias, not a primary RCT.
Methodological paper about equivalence trial design, not a primary RCT.
Observational incidence study, not an RCT comparing treatments.
Methodological paper about measuring inconsistency in meta-analyses, not a primary RCT.
PRISMA guidelines paper, not a primary RCT.
Review article about AED mechanisms of action, not a primary RCT.
RCT comparing phenobarbitone and phenytoin monotherapy (along with carbamazepine and sodium valproate) in adults with newly diagnosed epilepsy.
RCT comparing phenobarbital and phenytoin monotherapy (along with carbamazepine) in patients with partial complex epilepsy. Crossover design.
Trial focused on carbamazepine, does not compare phenobarbitone vs phenytoin monotherapy.
ILAE classification position paper, not a primary RCT.
Network meta-analysis of individual participant data, not a primary RCT.
Meta-analysis/multiple treatment comparison, not a primary RCT.
Study of patients previously on combination therapy, not a monotherapy comparison of phenobarbitone vs phenytoin.
Systematic review about pregnancy outcomes and neurodevelopment, not an RCT comparing phenobarbitone vs phenytoin monotherapy.
